extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in U.S. Congress, defense policy, and postwar public affairs
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing House action, debate, and provisions of a bill to unify the armed services and related national-security measures, plus related congressional actions (training plan, trusteeship, foreign aid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals of the unification measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan will help prevent future 'Pearl Harbor' disasters, cut military costs and curtail interservice 'back-biting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These benefits were asserted repeatedly during debate as primary justifications for the measure, although some members doubted economies would be achieved quickly or at all. Pearl Harbor references were used to argue for stronger unified command and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place all the armed forces under a single Cabinet officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Place all the armed forces under a single Cabinet officer (Secretary of Defense) — merge the present War and Navy departments and make the Army, Navy and Air subordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: House version would put forces under a single Cabinet officer; Senate prefers a Secretary of National Security. Debate touched on whether the Secretary should have Cabinet status and how much authority the new secretary should have; committee agreements preserve some service identities (e.g., Marine Corps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up a separate Department of Air
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a separate Department of Air (a distinct department and secretary for air matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the measure's structural changes; part of broader reorganization of service departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a National Security Council
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a national security council charged with keeping the President 'posted on the nation's strength' and recommending security measures after analyzing potential dangers; council to include the Secretaries of State, Defense, War, Navy, Air and the chairman of the National Security Resources Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council intended to co-ordinate the country's military and diplomatic program and advise the President on integrated strategic plans and use of national resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up a central intelligence agency (with restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a central intelligence agency for collecting and coordinating information on the military strength, developments and moves in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The House inserted a restriction—not in the Senate bill—to prevent the agency from exercising domestic police or espionage functions; House language also included stipulations to exclude internal security functions from the intelligence agency's operations to avoid domestic intrusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a National Security Resources Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a National Security Resources Board to advise the President on co-ordination of civilian, industrial and military mobilization in time of emergency and to keep a continuous balance account of the nation's 'resources, capabilities and risks in relation to our domestic, foreign and military policies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board would serve to maintain a continuous national inventory/balance and advise on mobilization planning and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put procurement of material under a permanent munitions/munitions-procurement board
rubrics_metrics.description: Put procurement of material for the armed services under a permanent munitions board or permanent munitions procurement board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure proponents said this would eliminate competition between Army and Navy in procurement and produce economies; opponents worried about concentration of power and loss of Congressional screening by the Budget Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place wartime Research and Development Board on permanent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the present wartime-created Research and Development Board on a permanent basis to take full advantage of the Army's and Navy's scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at institutionalizing R&D coordination across services and preserving wartime scientific collaborations for peacetime needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Marine Corps separate identity and Navy aviation arm
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee agreements spelled out preservation of the Marine Corps' separate identity and assurance that the Navy shall retain its own aviation arm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the measure reorganizes services under a single department, specific protections were negotiated to maintain certain service roles and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel budget/estimates through Secretary of Defense and the Budget Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates (budget requests) should be channeled through the Secretary of Defense and the Budget Bureau before reaching Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents of other language argued this preserves Budget Bureau screening and prevents Congress from being overloaded; a House move eliminated a provision that would let departments send estimates directly to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand a balanced armed-forces structure with integrated strategic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation demands a balanced armed-forces structure with integrated, strategic plans for obtaining full use of manpower, materials, scientific research and new developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proponents argued integration is necessary to use the nation's resources effectively in time of war and peace; debate emphasized planning for mobilization and strategic coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory military training — eligibility and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory military training of all American males upon reaching the age of 18, or after their graduation from high school; the subcommittee bill calls for six months of basic training for qualified male youths between their eighteenth and twentieth birthdays followed by six months of membership in an ROTC, National Guard or other reserve component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Youth still in high school when they become 18 may defer induction until 20; the plan follows President Truman's advisory commission recommendation; committee estimated about 850,000 trainees annually (Army ~618,000; Navy ~232,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory training — pay, allowances, status and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees would be paid $30 a month during their basic training and would receive additional dependency allowances of $50 monthly for one dependent and $65 monthly for more than one; they would wear regular service uniforms with distinctive insignia and would not be subject to actual military service except in time of national emergency; the legislation prohibits public nuisances near training camps and sale/giving of intoxicating liquor to any youth in training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The measure specifies administrative and disciplinary rules for trainees and attempts to limit the program's intrusion into ordinary civil life while providing modest compensation and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of Pacific island trusteeship — interim Navy control and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: United States to take over administration of captured central Pacific islands under a United Nations trusteeship; President named Admiral Louis E. Denfeld United States high commissioner; an executive order delegated interim civil administration to the Navy pending transfer to a civilian department or agency 'at the earliest practicable date.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order provides that authority to close areas for security reasons shall be exercised jointly by the Secretary of the Navy and Secretary of State; the trusteeship agreement requires legislation to place the plan into effect and conduct relations through the Secretary of State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air policy board mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: A five-member air policy board was appointed to study and recommend policies to obtain the 'greatest possible benefits from aviation.' Its tasks include: (1) study current and future needs of American aviation, (2) assess the nature, type and extent of aircraft and air-transportation industries desirable or essential to national security and welfare, (3) propose methods of encouraging needed aviation developments, and (4) recommend improved organization and procedures for government handling of aviation matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board is to be independent of military, manufacturing or transport aviation interests, given full cooperation of government agencies, and report recommendations before year-end; the President urged a multi-year outlook for aviation policy and possible creation of a standing body.

rubrics_metrics.name: House restriction: exclude internal security/domestic policing from intelligence agency
rubrics_metrics.description: House wrote in a restriction to prevent the central intelligence agency from exercising domestic police or espionage functions and to exclude internal security functions from the intelligence agency's operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stipulation was emphasized during debate as a safeguard against creating a domestic Gestapo or opening FBI files to general scrutiny; Representative Busbey and others voiced concerns about civil liberties.
